answer: For the AI persona Alex (synthetic reactions, not a real person): In the pre-fix flow, the homepage showed only hourly room rates, and the extra projector and service charges and final total appeared only at review, so the initially cheaper-looking room ended at a higher all-in total. In the post-fix flow, all-in totals and fee breakdowns were shown on the homepage, persisted during meeting naming and review, letting the persona select the genuinely cheaper all-in option. Both sampled flows use the same short sequence—choose room, enter meeting name only, review, confirm—with meeting time, 12 people and projector pre-filled and no payment details requested. Because frames are sampled, they do not establish elapsed-time change or a causal speed effect. Next design must preserve that fast path: pre-filled requirements, single name field, no payment step, and immediate review/confirmation while keeping all-in pricing visible throughout.
